weaknesses.title: A 300% sales claim with no baseline or method
weaknesses.why: 300% compared to what, over what period, and what was your part? An interviewer will ask, and a vague answer hurts every other line.

weaknesses.fix: Say what you actually did for the sale, and keep the number only with its real baseline.

weaknesses.title: Required job terms are missing from your resume
weaknesses.why: Recruiters search and filter by the posting's terms, and AI graders check each basic qualification against your resume.
weaknesses.evidence_quote: Strong written and verbal communication skills
weaknesses.fix: For each missing term you truly have, show it in a bullet about real work. If you don't have it, leave it out.

weaknesses.title: Some job terms are only listed, not shown in your experience

weaknesses.evidence_quote: Experience with SQL and Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP)
weaknesses.fix: Where it is true, mention the skill in a bullet that describes the work you did with it.

weaknesses.title: Your own part in the team survey is unclear
weaknesses.why: The survey is your strongest proof for this job, and it was a team of 4. Which part was yours?

weaknesses.title: Weak openers slow the skim

screening.label: Simulated screening check
screening.method: Overall = 40% file readability + 40% job-keyword match + 20% content signals, rounded to steps of 5. Weights are our judgment, not calibrated to hiring outcomes.
screening.precision_note: Scores move in steps of 5 on purpose. A 70 and a 75 are not meaningfully different. The counts and the issue list matter more than the number.
screening.disclaimer: This is a simulation, not a real applicant tracking system. Every employer sets up its own software, and none of the big vendors publish exactly how they parse or rank resumes. This check looks for problems known to break resume parsing and for job-description requirements your resume doesn't show. A high score doesn't guarantee an interview, and a low score doesn't mean a robot rejected you. Most automatic rejections come from application questions (work authorization, location, degree, availability), and no resume edit changes those.

limitations: We don't run Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, iCIMS or Taleo; their parsers differ by vendor, version and employer settings.
Our text extraction stands in for theirs (method: docx-xml).
The skills dictionary is finite, and AI matchers may credit related experience differently.
We can't see the application questions the employer set up.
Scores aren't probabilities and aren't calibrated against interview outcomes.
Column detection is limited to Word section settings.
Dates are read to the month; seasons are approximated.
The reviewers are simulated by Claude. They can be wrong, and they never saw the real applicant pool.
